subject: Integration follow-up: tool/function calling patterns & auth for Acme Health POC
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmehealth.com>, Tom Gallagher <tom.gallagher@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 15:15:00 -0800
Subject: Integration follow-up: tool/function calling patterns & auth for Acme Health POC

Hi Priya / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on the integration patterns we discussed. See attached slides and a lightweight MVP manifest (acme-mvp-map.yaml).

Key points from call:
- Goal: real-time triage assistant for clinician intake forms (low latency, PHI isolation, audit logs).
- Primary inference needs: structured extraction -> reranker -> tool call(s) (EHR write / task creation).
- Constraints: on-prem EHR connector behind customer firewall; strict tokenization/PII rules.

Recommended pattern for POC (high level):
1) SDK + auth: use Redwood SDK with mTLS + short-lived tokens from your KMS. We propose a mutual auth flow where Acme issues a signed exchange for the POC.
2) Routing: route sensitive requests to your Private deployment (VPC) and non-PHI traffic to Hosted with an auditable fall-back policy.
3) Tool calling: define explicit tool interfaces (openapi-like stubs) for: extract_entity, rerank_results, ehr_write, create_followup_task. Start with synchronous fan-out for extract_entity -> rerank then sequentially call ehr_write (or parallelize non-dependent calls).
4) Embeddings / reranker: host a small embedding index in your VPC for patient-scoped vectors. Reranker runs locally to avoid egress of PHI.
5) Error handling: best-effort retries for transient failures; guaranteed compensating actions for write failures (write audit + queue for manual reconciliation).

Open questions we need from you to finalize the POC manifest:
- Which EHR endpoints (FHIR paths) will we need write access to?
- Do you have an internal KMS to mint short-lived client certs or prefer Redwood-managed cert rotation?
- Expected per-hour QPS for triage during peak clinic hours?

Next steps / asks:
- Priya: can you share sample (anonymized) intake payload and a whitelist of FHIR endpoints by EOD Monday?
- Tom: confirm whether we can deploy a small inference node inside your VPC (t-shirt: 1 GPU) or if we need to run everything on-prem.
- Redwood: Ben and Marcus will produce an integration pattern doc + sample SDK snippet by Friday.

Attachments: 20280112-acme-postcall-slides.pdf, acme-mvp-map.yaml

Thanks,
Hannah

Hannah / Ben — appreciate the clear recap and proposed approach. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) EHR endpoints: we can provide FHIR write scope for MedicationRequest and Task to start (FHIR v4). Will send endpoint list + credentials for sandbox.
2) KMS: we have an internal HashiCorp Vault instance and can mint short-lived certs; prefer us to manage certs for now.
3) VPC deploy: we can allow a customer-managed node inside our VPC (we'd prefer Redwood to bring a containerized inference node).
4) Traffic: expected initial QPS is low (5-10 qps) with spikes to ~30 qps during morning intake.

On tool calling: we like the explicit tool interface idea. A couple of technical asks:
- Can Redwood provide a sample tool schema for ehr_write so our EHR team can validate?
- For reranker: can you confirm whether the reranking model can run on CPU for the initial POC (we may not provision GPU immediately)?

We'll share the anonymized payload and endpoint whitelist by Monday 16 Jan.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmehealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Integration follow-up: tool/function calling patterns & auth for Acme Health POC

Priya — thanks, that info is perfect. Quick technical notes and a sample pattern we recommend for the POC; attaching a small YAML manifest (acme-mvp-map.yaml) that maps tools and routing rules.

On reranker performance:
- We can run a lightweight dense retriever + shallow transformer reranker on CPU for your expected QPS. Latency target: <200ms p95 if colocated in your VPC and using local embedding index. If you see higher QPS later, we recommend moving reranker to a 1-GPU inference node.

Sample tool definitions (high level):
- extract_entity(tool_id: "extractor_v1", contract: {input: json, output: entities[]}) -> synchronous, idempotent.
- rerank(tool_id: "reranker_v1", contract: {candidates: text[], context: text}) -> synchronous, best-effort cacheable.
- ehr_write(tool_id: "ehr_writer_v1", contract: {patient_id, payload}) -> asynchronous write with acknowledgement + audit record.
- create_followup(tool_id: "task_creator_v1", contract: {patient_id, task_meta}) -> async, retry queue.

Parallelization guidance:
- Run extract_entity and initial candidate retrieval in parallel where possible. Reranker must wait for candidate set.
- EHR writes should be performed after the reranker decision; we recommend making the write an asynchronous call with a durable queue (Redwood can push to an SQS-compatible endpoint in your VPC) so failures do not block the user flow.

Error handling / compensating actions:
- Transient 5xx from EHR: retry with exponential backoff up to N attempts, then move to dead-letter queue and create a follow-up task via task_creator_v1.
- Permanent 4xx (authorization, invalid payload): surface to UI with clear error code and log full request (PII-stripped) to the audit log.
- Partial failures (e.g., write succeeded but post-write webhooks failed): ensure idempotency keys on writes and provide reconciliation endpoints.

Auth pattern (concrete):
- Use mutual TLS between Redwood node and Acme VPC endpoint. Tokens for API calls are short-lived (5–15m) minted by Vault. Redwood SDK will renew tokens transparently.

I'll pull these patterns into a short doc and sample SDK snippets (Node + Python) and drop them to the Drive link by Friday.

—Ben
